What changed in the current release. The version this guide was built for is shown in the footer.

KTPH002Connection logging was rebuilt to actually be reliableKTPH003 — KTPH004terminal loggingKTPH005 previously wrote every connection to one fixed path (so two connections open at once interleaved into the same file), had no compression, and rotated by KTPH006deletingKTPH007 the file at the size limit. Files are now named KTPH000, a fresh one starts every day (optional) and whenever the size limit is hit, nothing is ever overwritten or deleted by rotation, and each closed file is gzip-compressed. Old archives are swept by the date encoded in their name once the retention period (default 30 days, KTPH001 keeps everything) expires, and only korTTY's own log files are ever touched, so it is safe to point the setting at a folder used for other things too.

KTPH000The terminal log is now redactedKTPH001 — captured lines pass through the same redaction as the session journal before anything is written: the connection's own stored password and any replacement rules an organization's policy defines. Log files, and a log folder korTTY created itself, are set to owner-only permissions where the filesystem supports it.

KTPH000Quick Connect gained a Terminal log sectionKTPH001 — configuring logging in the Connection Manager and then connecting from Quick Connect with a different authentication method previously dropped the setting silently; Quick Connect now carries its own folder, format and compression controls and applies them to the session it opens.

KTPH000Fixed: XML and JSON logs had two document roots and never parsedKTPH001, rotation wrote the closing footer twice, up to 10,000 queued lines from just before a disconnect could be silently dropped, and output was split on line endings in a way that destroyed indentation and turned every progress-bar frame into its own log entry. All four are fixed.
Session journal: filtered export, named markers, page appearance and screenshot editingKTPH000

KTPH003Exports can now be narrowed downKTPH004 — the KTPH005export dialogKTPH006 accepts any number of time windows (an entry only needs to fall into one of them), a topic filter as literal text, a regular expression, or handed to the AI to select by meaning, and a marker filter (all entries, only marked ones, or specific markers). Times are parsed leniently (KTPH000, KTPH001, KTPH002 all work) and widened by an adjustable tolerance (± 5 minutes by default), so an approximate window still catches the entry that actually straddles it. A filtered HTML bundle is rebuilt rather than copied — trimmed capture log, only the referenced screenshots — so a shared export cannot leak the rest of the session; every filtered PDF, Markdown file and bundle carries a banner naming the range so nobody mistakes it for the complete journal.

KTPH000Markers are no longer a fixed four-value listKTPH001 — beyond the built-ins (None, Info, Important, Error) you can now define your own KTPH002named, coloured markersKTPH003, each degrading to one of the built-ins for older journals and for the error/important counts. Optional rules apply a marker automatically as entries are captured, matching a literal term or a regular expression against the entry's title, summary, note and excerpts, with precedence KTPH004your own choice KTPH006 a rule KTPH007 the AI's suggestionKTPH005 — a rule never overwrites a marker you set by hand.

KTPH000The journal page has adjustable KTPH001appearanceKTPH002KTPH003 — a colour scheme (six fixed palettes, the page's automatic light/dark pair, or a scheme derived live from your terminal's own colours), a text font and a monospace font, chosen from a toolbar popover and remembered for every journal korTTY renders afterwards.

KTPH001Screenshots can be KTPH002annotatedKTPH003KTPH004 — pen, box, an "Unreadable" tool that coarsens a region into blocks, and text labels, plus a note field, reachable by right-clicking a screenshot. Marks are stored as data and stay re-editable; the untouched capture is kept locally as KTPH000 and is never included in an export. This obscures a value in the rendered page, it does not redact it — use Search KTPH005 replace or a policy redaction rule to remove something from a journal for good.

KTPH000Selecting a time range got easierKTPH001 — inside korTTY the viewer's timeline can be switched into range-selection mode: click a first and a last entry to highlight the span between them and hand it straight to the export dialog, or collect several windows before exporting. The same selection is available from the edit-mode entry table via right-click.
KTPH000The journal's title is editable directly from the pageKTPH001, and a header button jumps between marked entries when a journal has any.

Only the current release is listed here, so the guide stays short in every language it is translated into. Every version is on the KTPH002GitHub releases pageKTPH003; the curated notes for earlier versions are kept in the repository, in KTPH000 and KTPH001.
